tagline: Through the marsh to the Gulf, then east along the cheniers.
intro: From Sulphur, LA 27 heads south through Hackberry into country sometimes called Louisiana's Outback, past the marsh of the Sabine refuge, and comes out at the Gulf at Holly Beach. There the road turns east along the shore on LA 82, through Cameron and out along the cheniers, old sandy ridges topped with oaks, to Grand Chenier.

Four wildlife refuges and 26 miles of natural Gulf beach lie along the way, and the alligators run up to 14 feet. The coast towns have been flattened by hurricanes more than once. After Audrey in 1957, some of the houses at Holly Beach were raised.

moments.title: Sabine National Wildlife Refuge
moments.text: The largest coastal marsh refuge on the Gulf, home to more than 200 kinds of birds, with a 1.5-mile Wetland Walkway looping out into the marsh.

moments.title: Holly Beach
moments.text: The Cajun Riviera, a row of beach camps built to be rebuilt. A 1991 swamp pop song allowed that there was no boardwalk, just seaweed, and a good time anyway.

moments.title: Cameron
moments.text: The parish seat at the mouth of the Calcasieu, wrecked by Audrey in 1957, Rita in 2005, Ike in 2008 and Laura in 2020. The library came back on tall stilts.

practical: Price Lake Road into Rockefeller Wildlife Refuge is closed from December 1 to March 1.
